hero_sub: Real download, upload, ping and jitter — no ads, no tracking, no accounts.
res_none_p: Run a speed test first and your report will appear here.
v_top: Excellent — ready for 4K+ streams and heavy downloads
v_mid: Good — HD streaming and smooth video calls
v_low: Okay — web browsing and HD video
about_lead: OpenSpeed is a small, honest internet speed test. No ads, no result database, no dark patterns — just the numbers.
what_p: OpenSpeed is an amateur, community-run speed test built on the open LibreSpeed engine. It measures how fast your connection really is: download, upload, latency (ping) and jitter, and shows your IP and provider. The list of test points is maintained openly on GitHub — anyone can add their own server.
how_p1: Your browser downloads and uploads random data to the selected test server for a few seconds and measures the throughput. Ping and jitter come from a series of small latency probes. Everything runs in HTML5 — no Flash, no Java, no apps.
how_p2: By default OpenSpeed picks the server with the lowest response time, but you can always choose one manually — useful when you want to test the route to a specific city or provider.
priv_p: Nothing is stored. Results live only in your browser for the duration of the session, and the only thing test servers see is the traffic of the measurement itself. IP and provider detection uses public geo-IP services and is never written to a database.
cred_p1: The measurement engine is LibreSpeed by Federico Dossena — free software under the LGPLv3 license. Test point backends are the original LibreSpeed PHP scripts.
cred_p2: The OpenSpeed interface, server list and site are maintained by the community at github.com/yuno-su/openspeed.
add_lead: The OpenSpeed test point list is open: if you run a server with the LibreSpeed backend, you can add it to the public list with a pull request.
req1: A publicly reachable server with the LibreSpeed PHP backend (empty.php, garbage.php, getIP.php) — or a compatible go / rust / node backend.
req2: Reasonably stable uptime: the list is shared by everyone, dead points are removed.
req3: HTTPS on the server is strongly recommended — an https site cannot test against plain http points (mixed content).
req4: Honest bandwidth: don't throttle the test files.
req5: One row in servers.php per test point, following the format below.
step1_p: github.com/yuno-su/openspeed — the server list lives in servers.php at the repo root.
step2_p: Copy any existing block in the array, change the values to your server's, keep the LibreSpeed file names as they are.
step3_p: We will check that the backend answers and the ping is sane, then merge it. Your server appears in the picker for everyone.
fields_note: Every block also uses the standard LibreSpeed keys dlURL, ulURL, pingURL and getIpURL — keep them matching your backend layout.
fd_name: Label of the test point, shown as a fallback
fd_provider: Sponsor, hosting or ISP running the server
fd_server: Backend base URL, must end with a slash
fd_speed: Port speed label, e.g. "1 Gbps" — leave empty to hide
fd_type: "dc" = datacenter, "res" = residential; empty = auto-detect via ip-api.com
tip_p: The server type (datacenter / residential) is detected automatically through ip-api.com and cached on the site host, so a freshly added server may get its tag a few minutes late. Ping in the picker is measured live from your browser.
tip2_p: Looking for more public LibreSpeed backends? A plain web search for "librespeed example" turns up plenty — probe each one (empty.php, garbage.php, getIP.php) and add only the ones you trust.
foot_open: Free and open-source software · engine: LibreSpeed (LGPLv3)
fd_url: Website of the provider or sponsor (with https://) — shown as a clickable link under the location
